meta.disclaimer: An unofficial student-made tool. Not affiliated with Minerva University. Always check official requirements at minerva.edu.
meta.privacy_note: Everything you enter stays in this browser tab. Nothing is saved or sent anywhere.

cycle.label: Undergraduate admissions cycle with deadlines from Nov 2026 to Mar 2027
cycle.deadline_time_note: Minerva lists dates only. This planner treats each deadline as the end of that day. Ask admissions@minerva.edu if you need the exact time and time zone.

rounds.name: Early Action (Binding Optional)
rounds.note: Binding option: if admitted, you must enroll and withdraw other applications within 10 days of your decision.

school_types.label: US high school (public or private)
school_types.default_busy_note: Thanksgiving and winter break are marked busy. Tap to change.

school_types.label: Local school outside the US, possibly without a counselor
school_types.extra_waiting_note: Your school may not have done this before, so school steps get 14 extra days.

school_types.label: Not sure
school_types.extra_waiting_note: Since you're not sure, the planner gives school steps 14 extra days to be safe.

planning.buffer_note: The plan aims to finish 3 days before each deadline, in case something goes wrong.

own_steps.name: Part 1: personal and academic information
own_steps.tip: Applicants under 18 also give a parent or guardian's contact details. You can save and come back later.

own_steps.tip: Timed. No preparation needed. Use a quiet, distraction-free place.

own_steps.tip: Timed. No preparation needed. Use a quiet, distraction-free place.

own_steps.tip: Timed. No preparation needed. Use a quiet, distraction-free place.

own_steps.name: Challenge: Divergent Thinking
own_steps.tip: Timed. No preparation needed. Use a quiet, distraction-free place.

own_steps.name: Written communication task
own_steps.tip: Explores your perspectives and experiences. Minerva lists 'written and verbal communication tasks' at about 20 minutes each but doesn't state an exact number.

own_steps.name: Verbal communication task
own_steps.tip: Explores your perspectives and experiences. Minerva lists 'written and verbal communication tasks' at about 20 minutes each but doesn't state an exact number.

own_steps.name: Accomplishments
own_steps.tip: Describe what you did and what you learned, with supporting documents, links or references. Be specific about your own role.

own_steps.name: Academic background section
own_steps.tip: Your most recent three years of academic records (can be from more than one school) and verification from a school counselor or equivalent official.

waiting_steps.name: School sends your academic records (most recent three years)
waiting_steps.done_label: I've asked my school for my records
waiting_steps.tip: Ask early. Your records may come from more than one school.

waiting_steps.name: School counselor or equivalent official completes verification
waiting_steps.tip: No counselor? See the local school guide for who could be an equivalent official.

waiting_steps.name: Translations of records that aren't in English
waiting_steps.tip: Minerva's admissions page doesn't explain translation rules. Before you pay for one, ask admissions@minerva.edu what kind of translation they accept.
waiting_steps.requirement_source: Not stated on the admissions page. Ask admissions@minerva.edu.

waiting_steps.name: Gather parent/guardian financial documents
waiting_steps.tip: If you're applying for financial aid: documents such as income statements and tax returns. Funding is limited, so earlier is better.

calendar.default_busy_note: Winter holidays are marked busy. Tap to change.
busy_rules: Your own steps are never scheduled on a busy day or a past day.
Busy days don't count as progress for school steps (records and verification), so those steps start earlier.

computer.requirement: Use a reliable desktop or laptop computer with a stable internet connection.
computer.no_access_note: You'll need a desktop or laptop for the challenges. Arrange one before your first challenge: ask your school's computer room, a public library, or a friend or relative.

start_page.question: What kind of school are you at?
start_page.intro: Answer one question and get a plan with start dates for each part of your Minerva application.

international.title: Guide for international schools
international.subtitle: For students at IB, A-level or other international schools.

sections.heading: Which records to send
items: Minerva asks for your most recent three years of academic records. These can include transcripts from more than one school.
Minerva also asks for verification from a school counselor or equivalent official.
Questions about predicted grades, IB or A-level results, or exactly which documents count? Ask Minerva at admissions@minerva.edu.

sections.heading: Working with your counselor
items: Tell your counselor early which round you're aiming for and its deadline. The planner shows the date to ask by.
Your counselor is the person most likely to provide the verification Minerva asks for.
Not sure what your counselor needs to send, or where? Ask Minerva at admissions@minerva.edu.

sections.heading: Timing around mock exams and predicted grades
items: Minerva's admissions page doesn't mention mock exams or predicted grades. Ask Minerva at admissions@minerva.edu.
Minerva says to do the challenges in a focused, distraction-free place. Avoid scheduling them during mock exam weeks.
You can save your application and come back later. You don't have to do it all at once.

us.title: Guide for US high schools
us.subtitle: For students at public or private high schools in the US.

sections.heading: Your counselor and records
items: Minerva asks for your most recent three years of academic records and verification from a school counselor or equivalent official.

local.title: Guide for local schools outside the US
local.subtitle: For students at schools outside the US without a counselor, or where staff have never done this before.

sections.heading: Step 1: Find your equivalent official
items: Minerva asks for verification from a school counselor or equivalent official.
If your school has no counselor, think about who handles official records: for example the principal, the registrar, or a head teacher.
Not sure if someone counts as an equivalent official? Email admissions@minerva.edu before your deadline.

sections.heading: Step 2: Ask them, early
items: Ask in person if you can, and give them the message below (printed or sent).
Tell them your deadline. Use the date the planner gives you, which leaves time for the school to act.
Give them Minerva's contact, admissions@minerva.edu, in case they have questions.

sections.heading: Step 3: What they need to send, and where
items: Your most recent three years of academic records. These can come from more than one school.
Verification from them as your school counselor or equivalent official.
Minerva's admissions page doesn't say exactly how or where the school sends these. Check the instructions in your application, or ask admissions@minerva.edu.

message.heading: A message you can give your school official
message.note: Replace the parts in [brackets]. If your school official doesn't read English, translate this message into your school's language first.
message.text:
Dear [Name of school official],

My name is [Your full name], and I am a student in [your class/grade] at [school name]. I am applying to Minerva University, and the application needs two things from my school:

1. My academic records for the last three years, sent directly by the school.
2. The school's academic form: a verification from a school counselor or an equivalent official. Our school does not have a counselor, so I would be very grateful if you could act as the equivalent official.

My application deadline is [deadline]. I will share Minerva's instructions with you as soon as I have them. If you have any questions, Minerva's admissions team can be reached at admissions@minerva.edu.

Thank you very much for your help.

Kind regards,
[Your full name]

translations.heading: If your records aren't in English
items: Minerva's admissions page doesn't explain what translations it accepts.
Before you pay for a translation, email admissions@minerva.edu and ask what kind of translation they need.
Start early. Translations can take weeks, so the planner schedules them as a waiting step.

computer_checklist.heading: Laptop access checklist
items: I have a desktop or laptop I can use (Minerva says a reliable desktop or laptop is needed).
The internet connection there is stable.
I can use it in a quiet place without interruptions for about 20 minutes per challenge.
I've booked time on it (school computer room, public library, or a friend or relative) before my first challenge date.
Not sure the computer has what the verbal communication task needs? Ask admissions@minerva.edu.

local.equivalent_official_notice: Not sure if someone counts as an equivalent official? Email admissions@minerva.edu before your deadline.
